rewrite.noticeThis: Yeshua calls his burial “the heart of the earth,” drawing an intentional parallel between Jonah’s three days in the sea creature and his own coming three days in the tomb. In ancient Jewish reckoning, any part of a day was counted as a whole day, anchoring the pattern of his death and resurrection firmly in Israel’s scriptures.

insight_issue: Rank 1: Correct the Deeper Lens textual claim. The insight asserts that English translations supplied 'Christ' as an 'interpretive addition... not a word actually present in this specific sentence.' In reality, the Byzantine / Majority Greek text explicitly reads 'ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με Χριστῷ', which the Textus Receptus and KJV translated literally. The insight should explain that earliest witnesses (P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus) omit Χριστῷ ('in the one strengthening me'), while later manuscripts made the referent explicit in the Greek text itself.

reason: The card's Notice This ignores the insight's Deeper Lens on synergei and the manuscript debate over God as explicit subject vs impersonal process, importing Romans 8:29 instead.

rewrite.noticeThis: The Greek verb synergei (“works together”) carries an ancient manuscript variation: some early copies explicitly name “God” as the subject, while others leave “all things” as the subject. The difference is vital: Paul is not celebrating an impersonal process where things just work out, but declaring that God Himself is actively at work in all things toward His purpose.
